claim: Data tiering automatically moves the least recently used items from memory to locally attached NVMe SSDs when available memory is completely consumed. When an item on SSD is accessed, ElastiCache asynchronously moves it back to memory before serving the request.
question: How does data tiering decide which items go to SSD, and what happens when an SSD item is read?

values.display: least recently used items from memory
asynchronously moves it back to memory

evidence.quote: Data tiering automatically and transparently moves the least recently used items from memory to locally attached NVMe SSDs when available memory capacity is completely consumed. When an item that moves to SSD is accessed, ElastiCache asynchronously moves it back to memory before serving the request, keeping hot data in RAM and cold data on disk.

claim: Assuming 500-byte string values, requests for data stored on SSD take an additional 300 microseconds of latency on average compared to data in memory. Requests for items already in memory see no latency penalty.

evidence.quote: Assuming 500-byte string values, you can expect an additional 300µs latency on average for requests to data stored on SSD compared to requests to data in memory. Requests for items already in memory see no latency penalty.

claim: Auto Discovery in ElastiCache for Memcached lets clients find cache nodes automatically when nodes are added or removed. Each Memcached cluster has a unique configuration endpoint that returns the current endpoints for all nodes in the cluster.
question: What is Auto Discovery in ElastiCache for Memcached?

evidence.quote: Auto Discovery is a feature in ElastiCache for Memcached that enables automatic discovery of cache nodes by clients when they are added to or removed from an ElastiCache cluster. Each ElastiCache for Memcached cluster has a unique configuration endpoint. When your client connects to this endpoint, ElastiCache returns the current endpoints for all nodes in the cluster.
